worldcombat.skill.skyattack.summary: Charge in place for a full beat (interruptible), then soar to a reachable high point and charge along a diagonal at the drop point locked at take-off as a heavy blow; you can pick a foe or just a world point, and an empty cast still takes off and dives. The drop point is fixed and never homes in, and the dive ends the moment it meets an entity or is stopped by a block. If it never rose above the drop point it only whiffs and never fakes a fall. A hit may flinch and interrupt it. High Dive braces longer and dives harder.
It charges along a diagonal at the locked point, dealing about %1$s damage on a hit; charge altitude is %2$s blocks and dive speed %3$s blocks/tick. Pick a foe or a raw point - an empty cast still takes off and dives at it. The drop point is fixed at take-off and never tracks, so a target that moves during the dive, or a dive stopped by a block, is missed.
Charging takes %1$s while standing still, with an impact radius of %2$s blocks; the charge can be interrupted, and an interrupted cast spends no PP - this move's open flaw.
On a hit there is a %1$s chance to flinch the target for %2$s, interrupting its interruptible action and preventing new moves and ordinary attacks during that time.

worldcombat.skill.skyattack.highDive.off: Low Dive: a faster, safer windup with altitude and power a notch lower.

worldcombat.skill.skyattack.growth.1: From level %1$s the dive power is %2$s and the flinch chance rises to %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.skyattack.use.0: Charge a beat, then drop a heavy blow from above
worldcombat.skill.skyattack.use.1: Reach a distant target over ground obstacles
worldcombat.skill.skyattack.use.2: Strike an airborne foe from above
worldcombat.skill.skyattack.preference.h: On: altitude x1.3 and dive power x1.12, at +6 tick charge, +3 tick recovery and +12 tick cooldown - a longer opening for a heavier blow. Off (Low Dive): a faster, safer windup with altitude and power a notch lower.
worldcombat.skill.skyattack.preference.a: It only considers taking off within this distance; smaller keeps it close, larger lets it open from farther away.

When on, an airborne target ranks higher only when this individual can actually rise above it with a clear take-off line; if it cannot climb high enough, all targets rank alike. When off all targets rank equal.
